newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's forces kill 40 guerrillas - papers.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's forces kill 40 guerrillas - papers.

text.p: Algeria's security forces have killed 40 Moslem guerrillas, including 12 shot dead after a gunbattle of several hours in Algiers, Algerian newspapers said on Thursday.
The 12 guerrillas were killed on Wednesday in an assault on their hideout near a mosque in Beaufraisier district on the northern edge of Algiers, said El Watan newspaper.
It said security forces also killed 25 guerrillas in Sour el Ghozlane, a Moslem rebel stronghold located 90 km (55 miles) south of Algiers. It gave no other details.
The newspaper Liberte said three more rebels were killed on Wednesday in Bab Ali suburb, south of Algiers, after a security force sweep.

Algiers residents said security forces were out in force carrying out search operations in guerrilla strongholds in Algiers and in neighbouring towns as the country geared up for parliamentary elections on June 5.
President Liamine Zeroual has vowed to ensure security for the elections.

Algeria has been without a parliament since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead. Violence erupted shortly after and about 60,000 people have died in the conflict.
